newsitem.title: MEXICO: Police dig up dirt in Mexico political murder.
newsitem.headline: Police dig up dirt in Mexico political murder.

text.p: Police and forensic experts probing a top-level political murder on Wednesday dug up the garden and took away soil samples from a house belonging to jailed Raul Salinas de Gortari, brother of Mexico's former president.

Officials at the Attorney General's Office said the operation followed a similar one on Tuesday at the house in northwestern Mexico City, and was linked to discovery of human bones last month buried at another Salinas house.
The digging was aimed at "taking samples of earth to carry out comparative studies of soil and soil density," one official said.

"The searches turned up additional elements" in the probe of the Sept. 28, 1994 murder of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, who was secretary-general of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), he added.

Raul Salinas, the elder brother of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, is in jail on charges of masterminding the murder of Ruiz Massieu, his former brother-in-law, with the help of PRI legislator Manuel Munoz Rocha.

Munoz disappeared days after the assassination. Prosecutors say they have information that Raul Salinas had him killed and are carrying out DNA tests to see whether the skeleton found at his house might be that of Munoz.

Officials said the house examined on Wednesday is registered in the name of Paulina Castanon, the wife of Raul Salinas who was herself arrested in Switzerland in November last year as she tried to withdraw money from a bank account held by her husband under a false name. She was later released.

Raul Salinas has also been charged with forgery and embezzlement following discovery of more than $100 million in foreign bank accounts, a private fortune amassed at a time when he was a mid-level government official in his brother's administration.
Carlos Salinas, who left Mexico in disgrace in March last year after his brother's arrest on murder charges, is currently living in Ireland.
